full_judgment: 2. Respondent No. 1-1st party on 1.4.93 lodged a complaint with the Officer-in-Charge of Baniachang Police Station against the present petitioners-second party alleging, inter alia, that he along with 48 others took lease of 40.53 acres of land in 6(six) plots in Khatian No.1 of village Pathalta for 5 (five) years from the Deputy Commissioner of Sylhet and Mutwali of K. B. Waqf Estate and that while they were possessing the said land by cultivating Irri and Boro paddy second party were planning to forcibly cut and take away the ripe paddy .grown by the first party. Thereafter on the basis of police report Magistrate started Non. G. R. Case No. 8 of 1993 and attached the disputed land and appointed a receiver. Both the parties filed their written statements claiming possession in the disputed land. After examining the witnesses and the documents filed by the parties the Magistrate by order dated 16.5.94 with-drew the order of attachment on 25.4.93, finding possession in favour of the second party. Subsequent thereto first party filed a criminal motion before the Sessions Judge, Habiganj. The learned Additional Sessions Judge set aside the order of the Magistrate. Being aggrieved by the same, second party-petitioner moved the High Court Division and obtained the Rule in Criminal Misc Case No. 1889 of 1994. By judgment dated 24.5.95 the Rule was made absolute after setting aside the judgment of the Additional Sessions Judge and direction was given to re-hear the criminal motion on merit. Thereafter Additional Sessions Judge considering the evidence of both the parties allowed the motion and set aside the order of the Magistrate and directed that the disputed land would remain under attachment till title is decided by the Civil Court. The Additional Sessions Judge also found that neither party could prove its possession. As already noticed, this order was affirmed by the High Court Division.
